'''''Parrotia persica''''', the '''Persian ironwood''', is a [[deciduous]] tree in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Hamamelidaceae, closely related to the witch-hazel genus ''[[Hamamelis]]''. It is [[native plant|native]] to the Caspian region of northern Iran (where it is called {{lang|fa|انجیلی}} {{Transliteration|fa|anjili}}) and southeastern [[Azerbaijan]] (where it is called ''{{lang|az|Dəmirağacı}}''). It is [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] in the [[Alborz]] mountains, where it is found mainly in [[Golestan National Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.visitouriran.com/blog/iran-wild-frontiers-golestan-national-park-and-tandoureh-national-park/|title=Iran Wild Frontiers (Part 1): Golestan National Park and Tandoureh National Park - Visit Our Iran - Discover Iran|website=Visitouriran.com|access-date=22 January 2022}}</ref>

[[Image:Parrotia persica Morton.jpg|right|thumb|Foliage]]

==Description==
''Parrotia persica'' grows swiftly when young, maturing in gardens to {{convert|30|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall and {{convert|8|-|15|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} broad, multi-stemmed and naturally somewhat congested but prunable to a single trunk up to {{convert|150|cm|0|abbr=on}} in diameter. The [[Bark (botany)|bark]] is smooth, pinkish-brown flaking/peeling to leave a mosaic of cinnamon, pink, green, and pale yellow patches in a similar manner to [[Platanus|plane trees]]. The [[leaf|leaves]] are alternate, ovoid, often slightly lop-sided, {{convert|6|-|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|4|-|10|cm|0|abbr=on}} across, with wavy margins; they are glossy green, turning in autumn to a rich purple to orange and brilliant red, often on the same tree.

The [[flower]]s are somewhat similar to witch-hazel flowers but dark red; they are likewise produced in late winter on bare stems, but differ in having only four rounded [[sepal]]s with no [[petal]]s; the [[stamen]]s are however fairly conspicuous, forming a dense red cluster {{convert|3|-|4|mm|abbr=on|frac=16}} across. The [[fruit]] is a two-parted [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]] containing two [[seed]]s, one in each half.<ref name=SOED>{{cite book|title=Shorter Oxford English dictionary, 6th ed.|year=2007|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-0199206872|pages=3804}}</ref>
[[Image:Persian Ironwood Parrotia persica Branches 2000px.jpg|thumb|Persian ironwood at [[Hershey Gardens]] in [[Hershey, Pennsylvania]]]]

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described as ''Hamamelis persica'' by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]] in 1830.<ref name = powo/> In 1831 [[Carl Anton von Meyer]] placed it in the new genus ''[[Parrotia]]'', which he named in honor of his predecessor at the [[Imperial University of Dorpat]], German naturalist [[Georg Friedrich Parrot]],<ref name=AZPLA>{{cite book|last=Coombes|first=Allen J.|title=The A to Z of plant names|year=2012|publisher=Timber Press|location=USA|isbn=9781604691962|pages=[https://archive.org/details/isbn_9781604691962/page/312 312]|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9781604691962/page/312}}</ref> who botanized in the Alborz on a mountaineering expedition in the 1830s.

==Cultivation==
''Parrotia persica'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental tree]] for its brilliant autumn colour and the smooth, patterned bark.<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Parrotia persica''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1382|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130423200159/http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1382|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 April 2013|access-date=25 May 2013}}</ref> As an uncommon, drought-tolerant garden tree of moderate size, it is prized for its striking autumn colour and the exfoliating bark that develops on mature specimens.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mortonarb.org/trees-plants/tree-plant-descriptions/persian-ironwood|title=Persian ironwood|website=The Morton Arboretum}}</ref>

Several [[cultivar]]s have been selected for garden planting:
* 'Horizontalis': semi-weeping, wide-spreading horizontal branching pattern.
* 'Pendula' (Kew Form): Compact, weeping, quite graceful
* 'Select': Young leaves have purple margins, otherwise same as species
* 'Vanessa': Upright, columnar habit

'Vanessa' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/54136/i-Parrotia-persica-i-Vanessa/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Parrotia persica'' 'Vanessa'|website=Rhs.org.uk| access-date = 18 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 72 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 17 April 2018}}</ref>
